chapters.summary: Lamentations chapter 1 portrays the desolate scene of Jerusalem after its destruction, as the prophet weeps over the people's sin and suffering.
keyPoints: Jerusalem, once thriving, now lies desolate like a widow, with no one to comfort her.
Because of the people's sin they are carried into exile, the temple is destroyed, the enemy triumphs, and God's judgment proves just.
The prophet's tears are his food; he calls the people to turn back and acknowledges that God is righteous.
chapters.application: When we face hardship, let us examine ourselves, confess our faults, and trust in God's righteousness and mercy, looking to him for deliverance even in our grief.

chapters.summary: Lamentations chapter 2 describes God judging Jerusalem in his anger, the holy city destroyed and the people in distress, as the prophet calls them to cry out to God.
keyPoints: In his anger God cast the glory of Israel down from heaven to earth, and the temple was destroyed.
Jerusalem's walls collapsed, her king and princes were cast off, and her prophets no longer receive visions from the LORD.
The people suffer famine and the sword, and the prophet calls them to lift up their hands to God and cry out to him.
chapters.application: When trouble comes, examine yourself and pour out your heart like water before God; seek his mercy in your grief, for his love never changes.

chapters.summary: Lamentations chapter 3 records the prophet's lament in the midst of suffering, yet in the end he finds hope and comfort in God's faithfulness.
keyPoints: The prophet describes in detail the suffering he has endured under God's wrath, as though hemmed in on every side.
In the depths of despair, the prophet reminds himself: it is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not - they are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
He calls the people to examine their ways and return to God, for the Lord will not cast off forever.
chapters.application: In hardship, let us do as Jeremiah did: count God's mercies, trust that his compassion is renewed every morning, examine ourselves, and turn back to him.

chapters.summary: This chapter laments the fall of Jerusalem, contrasting her former glory with her present misery, acknowledging that sin has brought this punishment, and pointing to hope in God's mercy.
keyPoints: The gold has grown dim, and the stones of the sanctuary lie scattered in the streets, a sign that all glory has departed.
Infants die of thirst and nobles waste away gaunt, painting a cruel picture of the famine.
The people's sin is greater than Sodom's, punishment has come, and the prophet calls them to repent.
chapters.application: When we suffer for our own wrongdoing, let us humbly confess our sin and look to God's mercy, trusting that he will not cast us off forever, but will grant grace to restore us.

chapters.summary: Lamentations chapter 5 is the people's prayer, crying out to God for restoration, acknowledging that they suffer for the sins of their ancestors, and pleading for God to turn again and show them favor.
keyPoints: The people acknowledge that their captivity came through the sins of their ancestors, and they now bear the consequences.
The chapter describes Zion lying desolate, the temple destroyed, and the people enduring humiliation and famine.
They cry out for God to look upon them, to turn again, and to restore them as in days of old.
chapters.application: In hardship, let us pour out our hearts honestly before God, confessing our weakness and wrongdoing, and hold fast to the belief that he is merciful and willing to turn toward us again, granting us renewal and hope.
